# Source Code {#sec-appendix-code}

This appendix contains the source code that is described in the thesis. All files are also part of the digital appendix (@sec-appendix-b).

## Verilog Design of the Flexlink Node {#sec-app-verilog}

The file `flexlink_node.v` contains the complete design of one Flexlink node, which is described in @sec-rtl. The same file is used for every node in the chain.

```{.verilog filename="flexlink_node.v"}
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// flexlink_node.v  -  ONE GateMate = ONE RGBW segment
//   LED data (uplink + downlink answer) and Count Segments in one file.
//   SAME bitstream on every GateMate, the ID comes from Count Segments.
//
//   UPLINK   (PC/PIC -> segments)
//      PC --TTL Tx--> [GM1 pin1] ... [GM1 pin3] --> [GM2 pin1] ... [GM2 pin3] --> (nothing)
//   DOWNLINK (segments -> PC/PIC)
//      PC <--TTL Rx-- [GM1 pin2] ... [GM1 pin4] <-- [GM2 pin2] ... [GM2 pin4] <-- (nothing, pull-up)
//
//   Packets (1 MBaud, 9 data bits):
//      Count   up : 160 | a | 176          a = segments before me, I pass on a+1
//      Count   dn : 1B0 | my_id | 176      every GM answers after a good count frame
//      LED     up : 100 | R G B W of GM1 (8 bytes) | R G B W of GM2 (8 bytes) | 176
//      LED     dn : 180 | my_id | temp | 176   every GM answers after a good LED frame
//
//   Send Count first, then LED. Before Count my_id is FF.
//
//   Pins (PmodA):  1 = up_rx   2 = dn_tx   3 = up_tx   4 = dn_rx (PULLUP)
//                  7..10 = SEG1..SEG4 (red, green, blue, white)
//   On-board D1..D4 = PWM of R G B W,  D5..D8 = my_id in binary
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
module flexlink_node #(
    parameter       CLKS_PER_BIT = 50,     // 50 MHz / 1 MBaud = 50 clocks per bit
    parameter [7:0] MY_TEMP      = 8'd40    // temperature, fixed for now (1 = 1 deg C)
)(
    input  wire       clk,            // 10 MHz on-board oscillator
    input  wire       up_rx,          // pin 1: from TTL Tx (GM1) / from previous GM pin 3
    output wire       dn_tx,          // pin 2: to TTL Rx (GM1) / to previous GM pin 4
    output wire       up_tx,          // pin 3: to next GM pin 1
    input  wire       dn_rx,          // pin 4: from next GM pin 2
    output wire [7:0] leds_n,         // on-board D1..D8 (0 = on)
    output wire       seg1,           // pin 7  : red
    output wire       seg2,           // pin 8  : green
    output wire       seg3,           // pin 9  : blue
    output wire       seg4,           // pin 10 : white
    output wire       vref_2v5
);

    // Flexlink commands
    localparam [8:0] LED_UP_SOP = 9'h100;   // LED data PC -> segments
    localparam [8:0] LED_DN_SOP = 9'h180;   // LED answer segments -> PC
    localparam [8:0] CNT_UP_SOP = 9'h160;   // count segments PC -> segments
    localparam [8:0] CNT_DN_SOP = 9'h1B0;   // count answer segments -> PC
    localparam [8:0] FL_EOP     = 9'h176;   // end of packet

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1) Clock: 10 MHz -> 50 MHz   (50,000,000 / 65,536 = 763 Hz PWM, above 400 Hz)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    wire clk_sys;
    wire pll_locked;

    CC_PLL #(
        .REF_CLK ("10.0"),
        .OUT_CLK ("50.0"),
        .PERF_MD ("ECONOMY")
    ) pll_inst (
        .CLK_REF             (clk),
        .CLK_FEEDBACK        (1'b0),
        .USR_CLK_REF         (1'b0),
        .USR_LOCKED_STDY_RST (1'b0),
        .USR_PLL_LOCKED_STDY (),
        .USR_PLL_LOCKED      (pll_locked),  // 1 when 50 MHz is stable
        .CLK270              (),
        .CLK180              (),
        .CLK90               (),
        .CLK0                (clk_sys),
        .CLK_REF_OUT         ()
    );

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 2) UART receiver (uplink), pin 1
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    wire [8:0] up_data;
    wire       up_valid;   // 1-clock pulse, new up_data arrived

    uart_rx9 #(.CLKS_PER_BIT(CLKS_PER_BIT)) u_up_rx (
        .clk(clk_sys), .rx(up_rx), .data(up_data), .valid(up_valid)
    );

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3) Decoder: for every symbol keep it or pass it on
    //    LED   : keep my first 8 bytes, pass on the rest
    //    Count : first data byte is a -> my_id = a, pass on a + 1 instead of a
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    localparam [3:0] MY_BYTES = 4'd8;   // 4 colours x 2 bytes. 8 = 1000 -> 4 bits

    reg        in_frame   = 1'b0;   // 1 between SOP and EOP
    reg        is_led     = 1'b0;   // this frame is LED data (100)
    reg        is_cnt     = 1'b0;   // this frame is count segments (160)
    reg        cnt_got    = 1'b0;   // count value already received in this frame
    reg        cnt_extra  = 1'b0;   // more than 1 data byte in the count packet -> wrong
    reg  [3:0] keep_count = 4'd0;   // how many of my bytes I kept (0..8)
    reg [63:0] frame_data = 64'd0;  // my 8 bytes
    reg  [7:0] temp_id    = 8'hFF;  // id from this count, taken only if the packet is ok
    reg  [7:0] my_id      = 8'hFF;  // FF = not counted yet, after count: GM1 = 00, GM2 = 01 ..

    reg [15:0] level_red   = 16'd0; // values shown on my LEDs
    reg [15:0] level_green = 16'd0;
    reg [15:0] level_blue  = 16'd0;
    reg [15:0] level_white = 16'd0;

    reg  [8:0] fwd_data  = 9'd0;    // symbol to pass on to the next GM
    reg        fwd_valid = 1'b0;    // pulse: put fwd_data in the queue
    reg        led_done  = 1'b0;    // pulse: good LED frame -> send LED answer
    reg        cnt_done  = 1'b0;    // pulse: good count frame -> send count answer

    always @(posedge clk_sys) begin
        fwd_valid <= 1'b0;
        led_done  <= 1'b0;
        cnt_done  <= 1'b0;

        if (up_valid) begin
            if (up_data == FL_EOP) begin
                if (in_frame && is_led && keep_count == MY_BYTES) begin   // got all my 8 bytes // Check: GM got all 8 of its bytes before updating
                    level_red   <= frame_data[63:48];
                    level_green <= frame_data[47:32];
                    level_blue  <= frame_data[31:16];
                    level_white <= frame_data[15:0];
                    led_done    <= 1'b1;    //only answer after a good frame
                end
                if (in_frame && is_cnt && cnt_got && !cnt_extra) begin
                    my_id    <= temp_id;    // packet was ok -> take the new id now
                    cnt_done <= 1'b1;
                end
                // EOP: pass it on, then act on the frame
                if (in_frame) begin
                    fwd_data  <= FL_EOP;
                    fwd_valid <= 1'b1;
                end
                in_frame <= 1'b0;
            end
            else if (up_data[8]) begin
                // any SOP: pass it on, start a new frame
                fwd_data   <= up_data;
                fwd_valid  <= 1'b1;
                in_frame   <= 1'b1;
                is_led     <= (up_data == LED_UP_SOP);
                is_cnt     <= (up_data == CNT_UP_SOP);
                cnt_got    <= 1'b0;  // cnt_got = 0  → I have NOT received the count value yet in this packet
                                     // cnt_got = 1  → I already received the count value
                cnt_extra  <= 1'b0;   // new frame, no extra bytes yet
                keep_count <= 4'd0;
            end
            else if (in_frame) begin
                if (is_led && keep_count < MY_BYTES) begin
                    // mine, push in from the right
                    frame_data <= {frame_data[55:0], up_data[7:0]};
                    keep_count <= keep_count + 4'd1;
                end
                else if (is_cnt && !cnt_got) begin // (Is this a count packet && I have not received a count value yet)
                                                   // count value a: I am segment a, next GM gets a+1
                    cnt_got   <= 1'b1;  // I have received the count value, so I will not process any more count values in this frame
                    temp_id   <= up_data[7:0];  // wait till EOP, take it only if packet is ok
                    if (up_data[7:0] != 8'hFF) begin
                        fwd_data  <= {1'b0, up_data[7:0] + 8'd1};   // next GM gets +1
                        fwd_valid <= 1'b1;
                    end                                             // FF: overflow, stop counting here
                end
                else begin
                    // not mine, pass it on
                    if (is_cnt) begin
                        cnt_extra <= 1'b1;
                    end
                    fwd_data  <= up_data;
                    fwd_valid <= 1'b1;
                end
            end
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 4) Uplink forward: queue -> UART transmitter -> pin 3
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    wire [8:0] up_q_data;
    wire       up_q_empty;
    wire       up_busy;
    reg        up_send = 1'b0;

    fifo9 u_up_q (
        .clk(clk_sys), .wr(fwd_valid), .din(fwd_data),
        .rd(up_send), .dout(up_q_data), .empty(up_q_empty)
    );

    always @(posedge clk_sys)
        up_send <= !up_q_empty && !up_busy && !up_send;   // something waiting + transmitter free

    uart_tx9 #(.CLKS_PER_BIT(CLKS_PER_BIT)) u_up_tx (   // sends to GM2 pin 1 from GM1 pin 3
        .clk(clk_sys), .send(up_send), .data(up_q_data), .tx(up_tx), .busy(up_busy)
    );

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 5) Downlink: my answer first, then the next GM's answers
    //    never mix packets, if I am passing on a packet from the next GM
    //    I finish it (till its EOP) before my own
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    wire [8:0] dn_data;
    wire       dn_valid;

    uart_rx9 #(.CLKS_PER_BIT(CLKS_PER_BIT)) u_dn_rx (
        .clk(clk_sys), .rx(dn_rx), .data(dn_data), .valid(dn_valid)
    );

    wire [8:0] dn_q_data;
    wire       dn_q_empty;
    reg        dn_q_read = 1'b0;

    fifo9 u_dn_q (
        .clk(clk_sys), .wr(dn_valid), .din(dn_data),
        .rd(dn_q_read), .dout(dn_q_data), .empty(dn_q_empty)
    );

    // my answer word by word
    //   LED   : 180 | my_id | temp | 176     reply_w 0..3
    //   Count : 1B0 | my_id | 176            reply_w 0..2
    reg       reply_pending = 1'b0;   // 1 = still have to send my answer
    reg       reply_is_cnt  = 1'b0;   // 1 = count answer, 0 = LED answer
    reg [2:0] reply_w       = 3'd0;   // which word is next

    wire [2:0] reply_last = reply_is_cnt ? 3'd2 : 3'd3;   // index of my EOP

    wire [8:0] reply_word =
        (reply_w == 3'd0)       ? (reply_is_cnt ? CNT_DN_SOP : LED_DN_SOP) :
        (reply_w == 3'd1)       ? {1'b0, my_id} :
        (reply_w == reply_last) ? FL_EOP :
                                  {1'b0, MY_TEMP};

    reg  [8:0] dn_send_data   = 9'd0;
    reg        dn_send        = 1'b0;   // pulse: send dn_send_data
    wire       dn_busy;
    reg        passing_packet = 1'b0;   // 1 = in the middle of a next-GM packet

    always @(posedge clk_sys) begin
        dn_send   <= 1'b0;
        dn_q_read <= 1'b0;

        if (led_done) begin
            reply_pending <= 1'b1;
            reply_is_cnt  <= 1'b0;
            reply_w       <= 3'd0;
        end
        else if (cnt_done) begin
            reply_pending <= 1'b1;
            reply_is_cnt  <= 1'b1;
            reply_w       <= 3'd0;
        end
        else if (!dn_busy && !dn_send && !dn_q_read) begin   // transmitter free
            if (reply_pending && !passing_packet) begin
                // next word of MY answer
                dn_send_data <= reply_word;
                dn_send      <= 1'b1;
                reply_w      <= reply_w + 3'd1;
                if (reply_w == reply_last)
                    reply_pending <= 1'b0;                  // my EOP sent, done
            end
            else if (!dn_q_empty) begin
                // pass on one word from the next GM
                dn_send_data   <= dn_q_data;
                dn_send        <= 1'b1;
                dn_q_read      <= 1'b1;
                passing_packet <= (dn_q_data != FL_EOP);    // EOP -> packet finished
            end
        end
    end

    uart_tx9 #(.CLKS_PER_BIT(CLKS_PER_BIT)) u_dn_tx (
        .clk(clk_sys), .send(dn_send), .data(dn_send_data), .tx(dn_tx), .busy(dn_busy)
    );

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 6) PWM: one 16-bit counter, one compare per colour (763 Hz)
    //    65535 = always on. LEDs off till the PLL locks.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg [15:0] pwm_counter = 16'd0;
    always @(posedge clk_sys)
        pwm_counter <= pwm_counter + 16'd1;

    reg pwm_red = 1'b0, pwm_green = 1'b0, pwm_blue = 1'b0, pwm_white = 1'b0;

    always @(posedge clk_sys) begin
        pwm_red   <= pll_locked && ((level_red   == 16'hFFFF) || (pwm_counter < level_red));
        pwm_green <= pll_locked && ((level_green == 16'hFFFF) || (pwm_counter < level_green));
        pwm_blue  <= pll_locked && ((level_blue  == 16'hFFFF) || (pwm_counter < level_blue));
        pwm_white <= pll_locked && ((level_white == 16'hFFFF) || (pwm_counter < level_white));
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 7) Outputs
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    assign seg1 = pwm_red; // For Pot: pwm_red * pot_value
    assign seg2 = pwm_green; // For Pot: pwm_green * pot_value
    assign seg3 = pwm_blue; // For Pot: pwm_blue * pot_value
    assign seg4 = pwm_white; // For Pot: pwm_white * pot_value
    assign vref_2v5 = 1'b1;  // 2.5V reference for the LEDs

    // D1..D4 = PWM,  D5..D8 = my_id (GM1 = 00 -> all off, GM2 = 01 -> D5 on)
    assign leds_n = { ~my_id[3:0], ~pwm_white, ~pwm_blue, ~pwm_green, ~pwm_red };

endmodule


// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// uart_rx9 : receives ONE 9-bit symbol (1 start, 9 data LSB first, 1 stop)
//   wait for start bit, go to the middle of the bit, then sample every bit time
//   valid only if the stop bit is 1
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
module uart_rx9 #(parameter CLKS_PER_BIT = 434) (
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       rx,
    output reg  [8:0] data  = 9'd0,
    output reg        valid = 1'b0      // 1-clock pulse, data is new
);
    reg rx_meta = 1'b1, rx_sync = 1'b1; // 2 flip-flops, rx is not in step with our clock
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        rx_meta <= rx;
        rx_sync <= rx_meta;
    end

    localparam IDLE = 2'd0, START = 2'd1, DATA = 2'd2, STOP = 2'd3;
    reg  [1:0] state   = IDLE;
    reg [15:0] clk_cnt = 16'd0;
    reg  [3:0] bit_idx = 4'd0;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        valid <= 1'b0;
        case (state)
            IDLE:  if (rx_sync == 1'b0) begin state <= START; clk_cnt <= 16'd0; end

            START: if (clk_cnt == CLKS_PER_BIT/2 - 1) begin       // middle of start bit
                       clk_cnt <= 16'd0;
                       bit_idx <= 4'd0;
                       state   <= (rx_sync == 1'b0) ? DATA : IDLE;
                   end else clk_cnt <= clk_cnt + 16'd1;

            DATA:  if (clk_cnt == CLKS_PER_BIT - 1) begin         // middle of each data bit
                       clk_cnt       <= 16'd0;
                       data[bit_idx] <= rx_sync;
                       if (bit_idx == 4'd8) state <= STOP;
                       bit_idx <= bit_idx + 4'd1;
                   end else clk_cnt <= clk_cnt + 16'd1;

            STOP:  if (clk_cnt == CLKS_PER_BIT - 1) begin         // stop bit must be 1
                       clk_cnt <= 16'd0;
                       state   <= IDLE;
                       valid   <= (rx_sync == 1'b1);
                   end else clk_cnt <= clk_cnt + 16'd1;
        endcase
    end
endmodule


// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// uart_tx9 : sends ONE 9-bit symbol (1 start, 9 data LSB first, 1 stop) = 11 bits
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
module uart_tx9 #(parameter CLKS_PER_BIT = 434) (
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       send,             // 1-clock pulse: send data now
    input  wire [8:0] data,
    output reg        tx = 1'b1,        // line HIGH when idle
    output wire       busy
);
    reg [10:0] shift     = 11'h7FF;     // {stop, data[8:0], start}
    reg  [3:0] bits_left = 4'd0;
    reg [15:0] clk_cnt   = 16'd0;
    assign busy = (bits_left != 0);

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (!busy) begin
            if (send) begin
                shift     <= {1'b1, data, 1'b0};
                bits_left <= 4'd11;
                clk_cnt   <= 16'd0;
            end
        end else if (clk_cnt == CLKS_PER_BIT - 1) begin
            clk_cnt   <= 16'd0;
            shift     <= {1'b1, shift[10:1]};   // next bit
            bits_left <= bits_left - 4'd1;
        end else
            clk_cnt <= clk_cnt + 16'd1;
        tx <= busy ? shift[0] : 1'b1;
    end
endmodule


// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// fifo9 : small queue of 8 x 9-bit values (first in, first out)
//   holds a value when the transmitter is still busy, so nothing gets lost
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
module fifo9 (
    input  wire       clk,
    input  wire       wr,               // put din in
    input  wire [8:0] din,
    input  wire       rd,               // take the oldest out
    output wire [8:0] dout,             // oldest value
    output wire       empty
);
    reg [8:0] mem [0:7];
    reg [3:0] wp = 0, rp = 0;           // 1 extra bit to tell full from empty
    assign empty = (wp == rp);
    assign dout  = mem[rp[2:0]];
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr && (wp - rp) != 8) begin mem[wp[2:0]] <= din; wp <= wp + 1; end
        if (rd && !empty) rp <= rp + 1;
    end
endmodule
```

## Constraint File {#sec-app-ccf}

The constraint file `flexlink_node.ccf` assigns the signals of the design to the pins of the GateMate evaluation board (@sec-hw-flow, @tbl-pins).

```{.bash filename="flexlink_node.ccf"}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# flexlink_node.ccf  -  SAME pin file for every GateMate
#
#   PmodA pin 1  = up_rx  (IN)  from TTL Tx (GM1) / from previous GM pin 3
#   PmodA pin 2  = dn_tx  (OUT) to TTL Rx   (GM1) / to previous GM pin 4
#   PmodA pin 3  = up_tx  (OUT) to next GM pin 1
#   PmodA pin 4  = dn_rx  (IN)  from next GM pin 2
#   PmodA pin 7..10 = SEG1..SEG4 (red, green, blue, white)
#
#   up_rx has PULLUP   -> open line rests HIGH (idle)
#   dn_rx has PULLUP   -> open line rests HIGH (idle), no data from a missing next GM
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 10 MHz on-board oscillator -> PLL
Pin_in  "clk"   Loc = "IO_SB_A8" | SCHMITT_TRIGGER=true;

# Flexlink lines
Pin_in  "up_rx" Loc = "IO_NB_A0" | SCHMITT_TRIGGER=true | PULLUP=true;
Pin_out "dn_tx" Loc = "IO_NB_A1" | SLEW=FAST | DRIVE=12;
Pin_out "up_tx" Loc = "IO_NB_A2" | SLEW=FAST | DRIVE=12;
Pin_in  "dn_rx" Loc = "IO_NB_A3" | SCHMITT_TRIGGER=true | PULLUP=true;

# On-board LEDs D1..D8 (active low)
Pin_out "leds_n[0]" Loc = "IO_EB_B1";
Pin_out "leds_n[1]" Loc = "IO_EB_B2";
Pin_out "leds_n[2]" Loc = "IO_EB_B3";
Pin_out "leds_n[3]" Loc = "IO_EB_B4";
Pin_out "leds_n[4]" Loc = "IO_EB_B5";
Pin_out "leds_n[5]" Loc = "IO_EB_B6";
Pin_out "leds_n[6]" Loc = "IO_EB_B7";
Pin_out "leds_n[7]" Loc = "IO_EB_B8";

# Segment outputs to the transistor driver stages
Pin_out "seg1"  Loc = "IO_NB_B0" | SLEW=FAST | DRIVE=12;
Pin_out "seg2"  Loc = "IO_NB_B1" | SLEW=FAST | DRIVE=12;
Pin_out "seg3"  Loc = "IO_NB_B2" | SLEW=FAST | DRIVE=12;
Pin_out "seg4"  Loc = "IO_NB_B3" | SLEW=FAST | DRIVE=12;

Pin_out "vref_2v5" Loc = "IO_NB_A4" | DRIVE=12;
```

## PC Test Program {#sec-app-pc}

The Python program `flexlink_pc_test.py` acts as the master in the prototype (@sec-hw-pc-program). It first sends a Count Segments packet and then an LED data packet, and it prints the answers of the nodes. Before the LED data packet, it sends the unfinished packet `100 20 30`, which is used for test C2 (@tbl-robustness).

```{.python filename="flexlink_pc_test.py"}
# flexlink_pc.py  -  PC -> TTL adapter -> GM1 -> GM2
#   1) count segments  -> each GM gets its ID, PC gets the total
#   2) LED data        -> LEDs change, every GM answers with ID + temperature


import serial, time

PORT = "COM3"                

#        R      G      B      W        (0 .. 65535)
GM1 = [65535, 32767, 49151, 40000]      # segment 1 : hot pink #40000 = 61%
GM2 = [10000,  25000,     40000, 65000]  # segment 2 : blue + a little white

# 9th bit is made with the parity bit:  MARK = 1 (SOP/EOP),  SPACE = 0 (data)d
def busy_sleep(p_seconds):
    end = time.perf_counter() + p_seconds
    while time.perf_counter() < end:
        pass    

def send(byte_list, ninth_bit):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    ser.flush()
    stop = time.perf_counter()
    #print(f"  flush took {stop - start:.6f} seconds")
    start_b = time.perf_counter()
    busy_sleep(0.00005)    # wait out the buffer used to write to usb  # let the previous bytes leave # Uses seperate threads.
    stop_b = time.perf_counter()
    #print(f"  busy sleep took {stop_b - start_b:.6f} seconds")
    start_1 = time.perf_counter()
    ser.parity = serial.PARITY_MARK if ninth_bit else serial.PARITY_SPACE
    stop_1 = time.perf_counter()
    #print(f"  parity change took {stop_1 - start_1:.6f} seconds")
    ser.write(bytes(byte_list))

# PC only sees the low 8 bits:  1B0 -> B0,  180 -> 80,  176 -> 76
def show(answer):
    print("  received:", " ".join(f"{b:02X}" for b in answer) if answer else "(nothing)")

ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 1000000, bytesize=8, parity=serial.PARITY_SPACE, stopbits=1, timeout=0.5)

# ---- 1) count segments:  160 | 00 | 176  ->  answer  B0 | total | 76 ----
print("count segments ...")
ser.reset_input_buffer()
send([0x60], 1)                         # 0x160  SOP count
send([0x00], 0)                         # a = 0 segments before GM1
send([0x76], 1)                         # 0x176  EOP

answer = ser.read(64)
show(answer)
ids = []
i = 0
while i + 2 < len(answer):
    if answer[i] == 0xB0 and answer[i + 2] == 0x76:
        ids.append(answer[i + 1])
        print(f"  segment ID {answer[i + 1]:02d}")
        i += 3
    else:
        i += 1
print("  total segments:", len(ids))

# ---- 2) LED data:  100 | GM1 RGBW | GM2 RGBW | 176  ->  answers  80 | id | temp | 76 ----
print("LED data ...")
data = []
for v in GM1 + GM2:
    data += [v >> 8, v & 0xFF]          # high byte first -> 16 data bytes

ser.reset_input_buffer()
send([0x00], 1)                         # 0x100  SOP LED
send([0x20, 0x30], 0)
send([0x00],1)
send(data, 0)
send([0x76], 1)                         # 0x176  EOP
answer = ser.read(64)
show(answer)
i = 0
while i + 3 < len(answer):
    if answer[i] == 0x80 and answer[i + 3] == 0x76:
        print(f"  segment ID {answer[i + 1]} : temperature {answer[i + 2]} C")
        i += 4
    else:
        i += 1

ser.close()
```

## Receiver of the Simulink Model {#sec-app-rxcore}

The function `RX_Core` is the MATLAB Function block of the receiver in the Simulink model (@sec-sim-receiver). It is copied here from the model file `GateMate_SingleWire_TxRx_RGBW.slx`.

```{.matlab filename="RX_Core (MATLAB Function block)"}
function [Frame_Out, Frame_Valid] = RX_Core(Serial_In)
% Simple single-wire 64-bit RGBW receiver
%
% Ts   = 0.25 ms
% Tbit = 1 ms
% 4 samples per bit
%
% Frame:
% Idle HIGH
% Start bit LOW
% 64 data bits, MSB first
% Stop bit HIGH

persistent active
persistent sample_count
persistent bit_count
persistent shift_reg
persistent latched_frame
persistent previous_value

if isempty(active)
    active         = false;
    sample_count   = uint16(0);
    bit_count      = uint16(0);
    shift_reg      = uint64(0);
    latched_frame  = uint64(0);
    previous_value = 1;
end

%% Default outputs

% IMPORTANT:
% Output only the last COMPLETE frame.
% Do not output the partially received shift register.
Frame_Out   = latched_frame;
Frame_Valid = false;

%% IDLE STATE

if ~active

    % Detect falling edge:
    % Idle HIGH -> Start bit LOW
    if (previous_value > 0.5) && (Serial_In < 0.5)

        active       = true;
        sample_count = uint16(0);
        bit_count    = uint16(0);
        shift_reg    = uint64(0);

    end

%% RECEIVE STATE

else

    sample_count = sample_count + 1;

    % Sample approximately at the centre of every data bit.
    %
    % Start bit occupies approximately samples 0...3.
    % First data-bit sample occurs at sample 6.
    % Then sample every 4 samples.

    if sample_count >= 6 && ...
       mod(double(sample_count - 6), 4) == 0 && ...
       bit_count < 64

        % Shift previous bits left
        shift_reg = bitshift(shift_reg, 1);

        % Insert new bit into LSB
        if Serial_In > 0.5
            shift_reg = bitor(shift_reg, uint64(1));
        end

        bit_count = bit_count + 1;
    end

    %% Complete frame received

    if bit_count == 64

        % Latch the COMPLETE frame
        latched_frame = shift_reg;

        % Update output
        Frame_Out = latched_frame;

        % One-sample valid pulse
        Frame_Valid = true;

        % Return receiver to idle
        active       = false;
        sample_count = uint16(0);
        bit_count    = uint16(0);

    end
end

previous_value = Serial_In;

end
```
